notes:
Top-line: mid-market productivity SaaS (collaboration + knowledge base). Started on Redwood hosted API for embeddings+chat in Oct 2025; now negotiating Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable throughput and data isolation. POC done w/ hosted -> saw 18% token-cost reduction after prefix caching and batching suggestions.

POC / demo takeaways: 
- Demo 2026-01-22 (FF-20260122-OXB-DEMO) — product team liked streaming/structured output and built-in usage analytics.
- POC round 1 (2-week pilot on hosted, then 3-day smoke test on dedicated staging cluster) 2026-02-08..2026-02-12 (FF-20260210-POC-ROUND1). Throughput target: 250 reqs/s peak for support assistant, p95 latency goal <= 350ms for short chat flows.
- Observed: KV cache reduced median token ops by ~30%; but p95 spiked on convoluted long context threads. SE PR recommended configuring per-route batching and profile-based kernels.

Pricing/packaging negotiation summary: 
- Customer preference: 12-month committed Dedicated SKU with staged ramp (Q1 pilot -> Q2 moderate -> Q3 full commit). Proposed commit tiers: 2 GPUs (pilot), 6 GPUs (steady), 10 GPUs (peak/reserved) with burst credit to 2x for 48 hours/month.
- Overage: propose gradual overage rate of $X (placeholder) / GPU-hour above commit; customer wants per-minute metering option for short bursts.
- Ramp schedule discussed: 3-month ramp to reach 60% of committed throughput, 6 months to full. They want a 30% discounted overage rate month 1 post-commit while ramp stabilizes.
- Billing: monthly invoice against committed capacity + measured overage. Customer asked for a clear amortization schedule to present to finance.

Security & compliance notes: 
- Requires SSO/SAML integration, customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, SOC2 compliance proof for Redwood.
- Data residency: US and EU separation for different customer segments; will push Redwood to provide regional routing and residency appendix.

Quotes / paraphrases captured: 
- "We need predictable bills and a clear path to scale without surprises — finance won't sign off on open-ended overage risk." (Head of Platform)
- "Burst is critical around major product launches; can't be throttled to death for 48-72 hours." (CTO)

Commercial asks from Oxbloom: 
- Firm 12-month committed price with clear ramp schedule and defined burst windows.
- Option to convert part of committed spend to annual true-up credits.
- SLA addendum for p95 latency for dedicated route and credit definitions.

Internal Redwood TODOs: 
- Follow up with legal on sample SOW + residency appendix.
- Sales to provide concrete $ numbers for 2/6/10 GPU tiers and detailed overage math by 2026-03-05.
- SE to deliver updated kernel/batching config doc and run two additional peak-sim tests in staging.

Current sentiment: hopeful but price-sensitive. Finance + procurement are tougher than engineering.
